knowledge:
- key_parameters: useREM=logical indicating whether to use a Random Effects Model (TRUE) or Fixed Effects Model (FALSE) in zScores and zScoreFDR ;; CombineExp=integer vector specifying which experiments in the list of ExpressionSets should be combined ;; nperm=number of permutations for FDR estimation in zScoreFDR ;; Score=metric to plot in CountPlot (e.g., "FDR") ;; kindof=direction of effect to plot in CountPlot ("neg", "pos", or "two.sided")
- alternatives: meta.summaries from the rmeta package is mentioned as an alternative for meta-analysis of arbitrary effects and variances, whereas zScores is tailored specifically to the Choi et al. (2003) method
- when_to_use: When combining multiple independent high-throughput (e.g., microarray) datasets that address the same biological question (e.g., comparing the same two phenotypes/conditions) to increase statistical power and obtain a consensus effect size
- pitfalls: Combining datasets just because they are on the same platform is not justified; they must address the same biological question ;; Failing to check for inter-study heterogeneity (using Cochran's Q statistic via f.Q) before choosing between a Fixed Effects Model (FEM) and a Random Effects Model (REM). If Q is significant (high heterogeneity), REM should be used instead of FEM

workflows.name: manual_meta_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform step-by-step meta-analysis of two-sample microarray data to calculate effect sizes, evaluate heterogeneity, and fit fixed or random effects models.
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate effect size d for each study using getdF. 2. Adjust d values using dstar. 3. Calculate variance of adjusted d using sigmad. 4. Compute Cochran's Q statistic using f.Q to test for heterogeneity. 5. Fit Fixed Effects Model (FEM) using mu.tau2 and var.tau2. 6. Estimate between-study variance tau^2 using tau2.DL and fit Random Effects Model (REM).
workflows.code:
d.Split1     <- getdF(Split1, Split1.ER)
d.adj.Split1    <- dstar(d.Split1, length(Split1.ER))
var.d.adj.Spli1 <- sigmad(d.adj.Split1, sum(Split1.ER==0), sum(Split1.ER==1))
d.Split2 <- getdF(Split2, Split2.ER)
d.adj.Split2     <- dstar(d.Split2, length(Split2.ER))
var.d.adj.Split2 <- sigmad(d.adj.Split2, sum(Split2.ER==0), sum(Split2.ER==1))
mymns  <- cbind(d.adj.Split1, d.adj.Split2)
myvars <- cbind(var.d.adj.Spli1,var.d.adj.Split2)
my.Q   <- f.Q(mymns, myvars)
muFEM = mu.tau2(mymns, myvars)
sdFEM = var.tau2(myvars)
ZFEM = muFEM/sqrt(sdFEM)
my.tau2.DL<-tau2.DL(my.Q, num.studies, my.weights=1/myvars)
myvarsDL <- myvars + my.tau2.DL
muREM <- mu.tau2(mymns, myvarsDL)
varREM <- var.tau2(myvarsDL)
ZREM <- muREM/sqrt(varREM)

workflows.name: automated_meta_analysis_fdr
workflows.intent: Perform an all-in-one meta-analysis across multiple studies to compute combined z-scores, estimate false discovery rates (FDR) via permutations, and visualize results.
workflows.stages: 1. Compute combined z-scores and meta-analysis statistics using zScores. 2. Plot combined vs original scores and IDR plot using IDRplot. 3. Estimate FDR using zScoreFDR. 4. Visualize FDR thresholds and gene counts using CountPlot.
workflows.code:
esets     <- list(Split1,Split2,Nevins)
data.ER   <-pData(Nevins)[,"ER.status"]
levels(data.ER) <- c(0,1)
data.ER<- as.numeric(as.character(data.ER))
classes   <- list(Split1.ER,Split2.ER,data.ER)
theScores <- zScores(esets,classes,useREM=FALSE,CombineExp=1:2)
IDRplot(theScores,Combine=1:2,colPos="blue", colNeg="red")
ScoresFDR <- zScoreFDR(esets, classes, useREM=FALSE, nperm=50,CombineExp=1:2)
CountPlot(ScoresFDR,Score="FDR",kindof="two.sided",cols=c("red",theNewC),main="two sided FDR", xlab="FDR threshold",ylab="Number of genes",CombineExp=3)
